captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 8. In this lesson: Three days in Hoi An.
Read a travel blog and identify informative and descriptive language.
Here are some new words. Itinerary. A plan of where you will go on a trip. Lantern.
A light in a container, often made of paper or glass. Ancient. Very old, from long ago.
And some more words. Cuisine. A style of cooking from a particular place. Souvenir.
Something you buy to remember a place. Tailor. A person who makes clothes to fit you.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: a plan of where you will go on a trip?
Now some grammar: Non-defining relative clauses. A non-defining relative clause adds extra information.
It goes between commas and uses who, which or where, not that.
For example: Hoi An, which is in central Vietnam, is famous for its lanterns.
For example: My guide, who grew up there, knew every street.
Now listen, and read along. Three days in Hoi An.
If you only visit one town in central Vietnam, make it Hoi An. This small riverside town,
which was once a busy trading port,
has kept its narrow streets and yellow merchant houses for hundreds of years.
Day 1: We explored the Old Town on foot, because cars are not allowed in the centre.
We crossed the 400-year-old Japanese Covered Bridge and stopped at a tiny café for iced coffee with coconut.
Day 2: In the morning we cycled through rice fields to the beach.
In the afternoon, a local tailor measured me for a jacket – it was ready the next day!
Day 3: Our guide, who has lived in Hoi An all her life, took us to a cookery class.
We learned to make cao lau, a noodle dish you can only really find here. Top tip: Stay until evening.
When the sun goes down, hundreds of silk lanterns light up the streets and float on the river.
It is unforgettable.
Another question. The video will stop. What was Hoi An in the past?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like itinerary, lantern, ancient.
You practised non-defining relative clauses. And you read Three days in Hoi An.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 8. In this lesson: We've been travelling for hours.
Use the present perfect continuous for actions that started in the past and continue now.
Here are some new words. Backpack. A bag you carry on your back. Exhausted. Extremely tired. Delay.
A time when something is later than planned.
And some more words. Scenery. The natural features of a place, like mountains and rivers. Hostel.
A cheap place to stay, often for young travellers. Landscape. Everything you can see in an area of land.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: a bag you carry on your back?
Now some grammar: Present perfect continuous.
Use have or has been plus the i n g form for an action that started in the past and is still happening,
or has just stopped and has a result now. For example: We've been waiting for two hours.
For example: She's tired because she has been walking all day.
Now listen, and read along. Notes from the road. 18 July.
We've been travelling for nearly fourteen hours, and I am exhausted.
The train has been delayed twice, and the air-conditioning has stopped working.
But the scenery has made it worth it.
For the last hour we've been climbing through mountains covered in tea plantations. Every few minutes,
the train comes out of a tunnel and the whole landscape opens up below us like a green sea.
My brother has been reading the same page of his book since lunchtime because he keeps looking out of the window.
We should arrive at the hostel around midnight. I've been dreaming about a hot shower all day.
Another question. The video will stop. How long have they been travelling?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like backpack, exhausted, delay.
You practised present perfect continuous. And you read Notes from the road. Now try the practice questions.
See you next time!

But the scenery has made it worth it. For the last hour we've been climbing through mountains covered in tea plantations. Every few minutes, the train comes out of a tunnel and the whole landscape opens up below us like a green sea.
My brother has been reading the same page of his book since lunchtime because he keeps looking out of the window.
We should arrive at the hostel around midnight. I've been dreaming about a hot shower all day.

B.ctx:
Three days in Hoi An
If you only visit one town in central Vietnam, make it Hoi An. This small riverside town, which was once a busy trading port, has kept its narrow streets and yellow merchant houses for hundreds of years.
Day 1: We explored the Old Town on foot, because cars are not allowed in the centre. We crossed the 400-year-old Japanese Covered Bridge and stopped at a tiny café for iced coffee with coconut.
Day 2: In the morning we cycled through rice fields to the beach. In the afternoon, a local tailor measured me for a jacket – it was ready the next day!
Day 3: Our guide, who has lived in Hoi An all her life, took us to a cookery class. We learned to make cao lau, a noodle dish you can only really find here.
Top tip: Stay until evening. When the sun goes down, hundreds of silk lanterns light up the streets and float on the river. It is unforgettable.
